a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

L5 records for related acidic NSAIDs show high permeability and no significant gut-wall efflux. Indomethacin had a Caco-2 efflux ratio of 1.11, naproxen had a rat intestinal permeability of 2.6 times 10 to the minus 4 centimeters per second, and fenofibric acid had a fraction absorbed of 0.95. AZD3582 showed at least 94 percent absorption despite intestinal esterase metabolism.

C175 shows that BCRP inhibition increased the bioavailability of GV196771, a structurally distinct acidic chloroindole. This is a mechanistic efflux caveat but it has no quantitative F value and limited transferability to carprofen.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for carprofen is present in the supplied records.
The closest high-F context, tolfenamic acid, was studied in cirrhosis patients, so its near-complete F may partly reflect reduced first-pass metabolism and may not fully transfer.
L5 records are for reference molecules, not the query. No query-specific gut-wall efflux or intestinal metabolism data are supplied.
C175 provides a mechanistic efflux example for a structurally distinct acidic chloroindole, but no quantitative F and limited transferability.
First-pass hepatic metabolism for carprofen is not directly assessed in the supplied records.
